text: Every scheduling job starts on this calendar. Once you know where things are, the rest of this series is easy.
Home is the practice calendar.
The one thing to remember: right-click a visit to see everything you can do with it.
Pick whose calendar you want under Primary Provider.
Today jumps back to the current week.
The arrows move a week at a time.
And back.
Day shows one day in detail.
Week shows the whole week.
Each day shows its points, its drive time, and points per drive hour.
A card shows the zone, the arrival window we promised, the pet and owner, and the reason for the visit.
A red R L means the family hasn't done their Room Loader yet.
Now the one thing to remember: right-click the visit.
Scheduling: reschedule, explore alternatives, add to the waitlist, view, edit or remove the visit.
Visit Prep: the Room Loader, euthanasia consent, and records from the previous vet.
On Visit Day: Jot prep, Start and End Visit, the encounter, and the On My Way text.
Patient opens the chart, a medical note, or a message.
Client opens the client and the bill.
Open Scheduling again,
and click View appointment for the details.
The arrival window, who booked it and when, and a history of every change.
The family's phone, email and address are right here.

The most common mistakes: reading the start time as the arrival time, and hunting through menus for something that's on the right-click menu. Remember: right-click a visit to see everything you can do with it.
